method.candidate_selection: All 50 POTENTIAL_NORMATIVE_OR_MIXED_OBLIGATION candidates plus the single AMBIGUOUS_SCOPE candidate from the source-gap register.
method.source_review: Pinned VCFv4.5.tex source lines and three lines of surrounding context on each side were re-read. Decisions distinguish reader obligations from producer recommendations, BCF-only rules, optional metadata, descriptive context, and future variant semantics. For mixed sentences, proposal-level normative force is split so MUST, SHOULD, MAY and optional metadata are not collapsed into one force label.
method.semantic_mapping: Direct mappings denote source semantics already captured by the cited canonical requirement. Related IDs denote partial/contextual relationships only and are not counted as complete coverage. Refinements preserve the existing canonical requirement and explicitly propose the missing condition. All proposals remain non-canonical pending cross-version reconciliation and review.
method.requirement_policy: Proposals are not inserted into the canonical ledger until cross-version reconciliation, atomicity review, schema validation and independent review are complete. No implementation or test status is inferred from a proposal.
method.modality_policy: MUST/MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY, recommendation, optionality and descriptive context are kept distinct. Recommendation-only statements are not promoted to hard rejection rules.

\subsection{Meta-information lines}
File meta-information lines start with ``\verb|##|'' and must appear first in the VCF file, before the header line (section~\ref{header-line}) and data record lines (section~\ref{data-lines}).
They may be either \emph{unstructured} or \emph{structured}.

An \emph{unstructured} meta-information line consists of a~\emph{key} (denoting the type of meta-information recorded) and a~\emph{value} (which may not be empty and must not start with a `\verb|<|' character), separated by an `\verb|=|' character:

proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A VCF reader rejects a file in which a ## meta-information line occurs after the #CHROM header or among data records.

records.rationale: Requires all ## meta-information lines to precede the #CHROM header and all data records. Existing REQ-000003 only places ##fileformat first; it does not state this broader ordering rule.

lines.text: \subsubsection{Information field format}
INFO meta-information lines are structured lines with required fields ID, Number, Type, and Description, and recommended optional fields Source and Version:
\begin{verbatim}
##INFO=<ID=ID,Number=number,Type=type,Description="description",Source="source",Version="version">

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: A structured ##INFO declaration contains ID, Number, Type and Description attributes.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader rejects a ##INFO declaration missing any of ID, Number, Type or Description.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: Source and Version are recommended optional attributes on ##INFO declarations; their absence is valid.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader accepts an ##INFO declaration without Source and/or Version and preserves them when supplied.

records.rationale: The source combines mandatory INFO declaration attributes (ID, Number, Type, Description) with recommended optional Source and Version attributes. These have different normative force and must not be encoded as one all-required rule.

records.source_excerpt: For example, if the INFO field contains a single number, then this value must be $1$; if the INFO field describes a pair of numbers, then this value must be $2$ and so on.

lines.text: Possible Types for INFO fields are: Integer, Float, Flag, Character, and String.
The Number entry is an Integer that describes the number of values that can be included with the INFO field.
For example, if the INFO field contains a single number, then this value must be $1$; if the INFO field describes a pair of numbers, then this value must be $2$ and so on.
There are also certain special characters used to define special cases:

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: A field declared with a non-negative integer Number=n has exactly n values when present.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader validates value cardinality against the field declaration for arbitrary INFO and FORMAT tags.

records.rationale: Defines fixed integer Number cardinality: a field declared Number=n has exactly n values. Existing reserved-field rows record individual key metadata but do not enforce generic cardinality for arbitrary declared INFO/FORMAT fields.

proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader rejects a contig declaration or CHROM identifier that collides with a reserved symbolic allele token.

records.rationale: Contig identifiers must not collide with reserved symbolic allele names. Prevents ambiguity between reference names and symbolic ALT syntax.

lines.text: \item REF --- reference base(s): Each base must be one of A,C,G,T,N (case insensitive).
Multiple bases are permitted.

If any of the ALT alleles is a symbolic allele (an angle-bracketed ID String ``$<$ID$>$'') then the padding base is required and POS denotes the coordinate of the base preceding the polymorphism.
The exception to this is the $<$*$>$ symbolic allele for which the reference call interval includes the POS base.
Tools processing VCF files are not required to preserve case in the REF allele Strings. (String, Required).

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: A simple insertion or deletion is represented with a padding base preceding the variant, with POS identifying that padding base.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader validates the anchor-base representation and coordinate span for ordinary simple insertions/deletions.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: For a simple insertion or deletion at contig position 1, the padding base follows the variant and POS identifies that following base.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: Boundary tests at POS=1 validate right-padding without an impossible preceding base.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: For complex substitutions or other alleles where every allele string is non-empty, padding is not required but is permitted.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader accepts both permitted padded and unpadded complex alleles without changing their biological sequence.

records.rationale: The sentence contains the ordinary simple-indel anchor rule, a contig-position-1 exception, and a distinct permission that complex substitutions with non-empty alleles need not be padded. These are separate behaviors and must be split.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: For any symbolic ALT other than <*>, the required padding base precedes the polymorphism and POS identifies that preceding base.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader validates symbolic-ALT padding against the exact construct class and does not apply this generic rule to the VCFv4.5 <*> exception.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: The VCFv4.5 <*> unspecified allele uses the reference-call interval convention in which the POS base is included in the reference-call interval.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A gVCF parser distinguishes <*> from * and validates the reference-block start convention.

records.rationale: The generic symbolic-ALT padding rule and the <*> reference-block exception must be separated. The exception is specifically important for gVCF and cannot be generalized to the spanning-deletion '*' allele.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: When a VCF producer uses a reference sequence containing IUPAC ambiguity codes outside the VCF REF alphabet, it converts each ambiguous reference base to the alphabetically first concrete base before emitting the VCF REF allele.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: An upstream producer conformance test verifies the prescribed conversion for each unsupported IUPAC ambiguity symbol; SIRALOOM's reader never silently rewrites incoming REF values.

records.rationale: This is a normative producer-side conversion rule for ambiguous underlying reference sequences, not an additional reader-side input rule. Preserve it as an upstream producer/reference-provenance requirement. Incoming VCF REF is already constrained to A/C/G/T/N by L403; SIRALOOM must not silently rewrite user-supplied REF alleles to an alphabetically selected base.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: A sequence ALT allele is a non-empty string over A,C,G,T,N, case-insensitively; '*' is the spanning-deletion allele and '.' denotes no alternate allele.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader parses sequence alleles, preserves '*' as an overlapping-deletion marker, and does not treat it as an ordinary sequence allele.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: The <*> allele is a distinct unspecified/reference-confidence allele and is not an ordinary clinical alternate allele.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: The gVCF parser recognizes <*> as a reference-confidence construct and routes it to reference-block logic.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: Symbolic SV alleles and breakend replacement strings are recognized as distinct ALT classes and are not interpreted as ordinary short sequence alleles.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: Phase 1 preserves their original records and routes them to the retained future SV/BND workstream.

records.rationale: ALT grammar combines sequence alleles, spanning-deletion '*', missing '.', unspecified <*> reference-confidence allele, symbolic SV alleles and breakend strings. Phase 1 must distinguish all classes, process small-variant alleles and '*' correctly, and route unsupported symbolic SV/BND without pretending they are malformed.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: A record with no alternate alleles represents ALT using the missing marker '.'.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader rejects an empty ALT value and validates '.' as the no-alternate representation.

If ALT is `.' (no variant) then this is $-10log_{10}$ prob(variant), and if ALT is not `.' this is $-10log_{10}$ prob(no variant).
If unknown, the MISSING value must be specified. (Float)
\item FILTER --- filter status: PASS if this position has passed all filters, i.e., a call is made at this position.

Otherwise, if the site has not passed all filters, a semicolon-separated list of codes for filters that fail. e.g.\ ``q10;s50'' might indicate that at this site the quality is below 10 and the number of samples with data is below 50\% of the total number of samples.
`0' is reserved and must not be used as a filter String.

proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader accepts numeric QUAL or '.', and rejects nonnumeric or empty QUAL values.

records.rationale: QUAL is Float and unknown quality must be represented with the missing marker. Existing registry does not capture QUAL field type/missing semantics.

Each subfield consists of a short \emph{key} with optional \emph{values} in the format: key[=value[,\,\ldots,value]].

proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader preserves the distinction between FILTER='.' (not applied), FILTER='PASS' (applied and passed), and declared failing filter IDs.

\item INFO --- additional information: Semicolon-separated series of additional information fields, or the MISSING value `{\tt .}'\ if none are present.
Each subfield consists of a short \emph{key} with optional \emph{values} in the format: key[=value[,\,\ldots,value]].

Literal semicolon (`{\tt ;}') and equals sign (`{\tt =}') characters are not permitted in these values, and literal commas (`{\tt ,}') are permitted only as delimiters for lists of values; characters with special meaning can be encoded using percent encoding, see Section~\ref{character-encoding}.
Space characters are allowed in values.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: Each INFO entry is a key optionally followed by '=' and one or more comma-delimited values; semicolon separates entries and '.' denotes no INFO entries.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader parses INFO keys and values without conflating comma, semicolon or equals delimiters and preserves missing versus flag entries.

records.rationale: Defines INFO subfield grammar and optional value/list structure. Existing encoding requirements cover escaped characters but not the complete key[=value,...] grammar.

records.source_excerpt: INFO keys must match the regular expression \texttt{\^{}([A-Za-z\_][0-9A-Za-z\_.]*|1000G)\$}, please note that ``1000G'' is allowed as a special legacy value.

lines.text: Literal semicolon (`{\tt ;}') and equals sign (`{\tt =}') characters are not permitted in these values, and literal commas (`{\tt ,}') are permitted only as delimiters for lists of values; characters with special meaning can be encoded using percent encoding, see Section~\ref{character-encoding}.
Space characters are allowed in values.
INFO keys must match the regular expression \texttt{\^{}([A-Za-z\_][0-9A-Za-z\_.]*|1000G)\$}, please note that ``1000G'' is allowed as a special legacy value.
Duplicate keys are not allowed.
Arbitrary keys are permitted, although those listed in Table~\ref{table:reserved-info} and described below are reserved (albeit optional).

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: INFO keys match the VCFv4.5 key grammar, including the explicit legacy exception '1000G'.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader accepts keys in the defined grammar and rejects keys outside it.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: An INFO field does not contain duplicate keys.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader rejects repeated INFO keys within one record.

records.rationale: The line contains two independently testable constraints: the allowed INFO key regular expression (including legacy 1000G) and the prohibition on duplicate INFO keys in a record.

records.source_excerpt: This is a computed field that, when present, must be set to the maximum end reference position (1-based) of:

lines.text: \item END: Deprecated.
Retained for backwards compatibility with  earlier versions of VCF and older VCF indexing software which rely on this field being present.
This is a computed field that, when present, must be set to the maximum end reference position (1-based) of:
the position of the final base of the REF allele,
the end position corresponding to the SVLEN of a symbolic SV allele,
and the end positions calculated from FORMAT LEN for the $<$*$>$ symbolic allele.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: When INFO END is present, it equals the maximum 1-based end coordinate implied by REF, symbolic SVLEN where applicable, and FORMAT LEN for <*> reference blocks.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader validates END against all applicable record components; for ordinary sequence-only variants it at minimum agrees with the REF span, and for gVCF it accounts for the sample-specific LEN semantics.

records.rationale: Existing requirements capture END deprecation and a backwards-compatibility inference from END to LEN, but not the computed END value itself. This sentence is a maximum across REF end, symbolic SVLEN end, and <*> FORMAT LEN end; create a distinct conditional requirement and retain structural branches for future SV.

records.source_excerpt: If any local-allele field is present, LAA must also be present and precede all fields other than GT.

lines.text: First a FORMAT field is given specifying the data types and order (colon-separated FORMAT keys matching the regular expression \texttt{\^{}[A-Za-z\_][0-9A-Za-z\_.]*\$}, duplicate keys are not allowed).
This is followed by one data block per sample, with the colon-separated data corresponding to the types specified in the format.
The first key must always be the genotype (GT) if it is present.
If any local-allele field is present, LAA must also be present and precede all fields other than GT.
There are no required keys.
Additional Genotype keys can be defined in the meta-information, however, software support for them is not guaranteed.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: When local-allele fields are present, LAA occurs immediately after GT if GT is present, and before all other FORMAT fields.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A reader validates LAA ordering while preserving the independent GT-first rule.

records.rationale: REQ-000053 covers the LAA-presence dependency and REQ-000019 covers GT-first. The additional requirement that LAA precede all other non-GT fields is not covered and needs its own atomic requirement.

records.source_excerpt: It is recommended that VCF libraries provide an API in which local allele encoding can be abstracted away from the API consumer and values accessed through their corresponding non-local key.

lines.text: Due to BCF encoding empty vectors as missing, implementation-defined Number=LA local-allele fields should not be used if distinguishing between zero-length data and missing data is required at REF-only sites.
It is recommended that VCF libraries provide an API in which local allele encoding can be abstracted away from the API consumer and values accessed through their corresponding non-local key.

\item LPL: is a list of $n \choose \mathrm{Ploidy}$ integers giving phred-scaled genotype likelihoods (rounded to the closest integer; as per PL) for all possible genotypes given the set of alleles defined in the LAA local alleles.
The precise ordering is defined in the GL paragraph.

records.rationale: This is explicitly an API design recommendation for VCF libraries, not a file-format conformance obligation. Do not create a parser rejection rule from it.

records.source_excerpt: Values must be between 0 and 1 and indicate how prevalent the modified base is in the sample.

lines.text: The alias keys M5mC, M5hmC, M5fC, M5caC, M5hmU, M5fU, M5caU, M6mA, M8oxoG, and MxaoN should be used instead of their corresponding ChEBI keys.
Values must be between 0 and 1 and indicate how prevalent the modified base is in the sample.
When base modification information is present in the FORMAT field of a reference block record, the base modification information apply to all applicable bases covered by that reference block.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: Base-modification M values are in the closed interval [0,1] and represent prevalence in the sample.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A future base-modification parser rejects values below 0 or above 1.

records.rationale: The 0..1 range constrains base-modification M values. REQ-000075 records Number=M cardinality but not value range. This is a valid future base-modification semantic requirement, not a Phase 1 SNV/indel or gVCF reference-block acceptance requirement unless base modifications are explicitly supported.

records.source_excerpt: \item The INFO and FORMAT CN fields should be present for $<$CNV:TR$>$ records (as they are $<$CNV$>$ records) and, when present, must correspond to the sample allelic length divided by the reference allelic length.

lines.text: \item When both $<$CNV:TR$>$ and the equivalent non-symbolic records are present, the $<$CNV:TR$>$ should approximately encode the sequence but is not required to encode the sequence exactly.
For example, SNVs and indels may be omitted in the $<$CNV:TR$>$ record.
\item Variant callers which do not report allele-specific tandem repeats should use a single $<$CNV:TR$>$ ALT allele and the missing genotype for the GT field (for example, $./.$ if diploid).

\item The INFO and FORMAT CN fields should be present for $<$CNV:TR$>$ records (as they are $<$CNV$>$ records) and, when present, must correspond to the sample allelic length divided by the reference allelic length.
Note that CN FORMAT field represents the overall copy number and the INFO CN the allele-specific copy number.

\item When benchmarking tandem repeats, the $<$CNV:TR$>$ interval provides a region over which a set of (preferably phased) non-symbolic records can be compared against for length and sequence composition.
\item RN encodes the number of records for each allele in the RUS, RUL, RUC, RB fields.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: INFO and FORMAT CN are recommended for <CNV:TR> records.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A future CNV/TR implementation accepts their absence without treating it as a format violation.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: When INFO CN or FORMAT CN is present for <CNV:TR>, its value corresponds to sample allelic length divided by reference allelic length, with INFO CN allele-specific and FORMAT CN overall.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A future CNV/TR implementation validates the appropriate ratio semantics and distinguishes INFO versus FORMAT scope.

records.rationale: The source mixes a SHOULD for presence of INFO/FORMAT CN with a MUST consistency rule conditional on those fields being present. The CN semantics are future CNV/TR scope; existing REQ-000096 addresses a different SVLEN consistency condition and is not a substitute.

records.source_excerpt: \item RUS or RUL must be specified for each $<$CNV:TR$>$.

lines.text: Conceptually, this a mechanism to encode a list-of-list with flat list format used in VCF.
\item STRs should use RUS, whereas VNTRs should use RUL to ensure the VCF records are not excessively large.
\item RUL should be omitted when RUS is present (as it is redundant when RS is present).
\item RUS or RUL must be specified for each $<$CNV:TR$>$.

\item Support for multiple levels of repeat nesting (such as STRs within VNTRs) is limited to the RUL repeat unit length field which allows the overall length of each top-level repeat unit to be encoded.
\item The POS and SVLEN of $<$CNV:TR$>$ records should match the STR/VNTR reference catalog sizes for catalog-based callers.
\item Variant normalisation has limited utility in regions of low complexity as almost identical haplotypes can have very different normalised representations.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: Each <CNV:TR> allele specifies at least one of RUS or RUL.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A future tandem-repeat parser rejects a <CNV:TR> allele lacking both RUS and RUL.

records.rationale: RUS or RUL is mandatory for each <CNV:TR> allele. This is a future tandem-repeat semantic requirement and must be retained rather than implemented in the Phase 1 small-variant release.

proposed_atomic_requirements.atomic_statement: For <CNV:TR> alleles, RN may be omitted when no allele has more than one repeat sequence; RN must be specified when any <CNV:TR> allele has RN greater than 1.
proposed_atomic_requirements.observable_acceptance_condition: A future tandem-repeat validator accepts omission of RN for single-repeat alleles and rejects omission when any allele requires RN greater than 1, while preserving the existing default of one when RN is absent.

records.rationale: This condition refines the existing RN default/absence rule: RN may be omitted when each relevant allele has at most one repeat record; RN is required when any <CNV:TR> allele has RN greater than 1. Existing REQ-000091 should be amended or explicitly cross-referenced, not duplicated.
